run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T04:43:40Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for service_name=frontend-proxy fires because spans of frontend-proxy operation "ingress" carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR: Prometheus shows ERROR-span increase values between about 2.1 and 15.8 spans per 10-minute lookback across 04:15–05:02, and the computed 5-minute ingress error ratio peaked at 0.0033 (0.33%) at 04:38:40 (evidence 54fa85b3, 9c9b8e9a). The frontend-proxy access log explains the failures: requests routed to the frontend upstream returned 503 with response flag UC and detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, sporadically from 04:13:34 through 04:51:45 (evidence 395aa463, 99dab9bb9, 99238777, 990a0ac6). Sampled traces of two such 503s show load-generator GET 503 -> frontend-proxy ingress 503 -> frontend-proxy "router frontend egress" span with error=true and http.status_code 0, with no frontend span in those traces, i.e. the upstream side closed the connection without answering (evidence 9096f650). A separate, time-limited contributor is visible at 04:36:15–04:36:19: six HTTP 500 "via_upstream" responses from frontend for /api/products/* and /api/checkout, while Deployment product-catalog was being rolled (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T04:36:15Z, new ReplicaSet 04:36:15, new pod Started 04:36:18, old pod Killing and old ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete at 04:36:19); frontend's own error spans (GET, POST, POST /api/checkout, executing api route /api/checkout, tcp.connect) are non-zero only in that period (evidence 689942e0, 55792f13, 73cbb951, cda92c95, bab12daa). frontend-proxy itself is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and only 3–5% CFS throttling, so the errors are observed at frontend-proxy but originate on the frontend-facing hop (evidence c016a76f, eb8148d0). The exact reason the frontend terminates those connections could not be established: frontend logs are not retrievable and its keep-alive/timeout configuration is baked into the image. The flagd fault-injection candidate productCatalogFailure is set to variant "on" in flagd-config, but the observed failure path (connection terminations plus a multi-product 500 burst at the pod swap) does not match a single-product failure and no product-catalog ERROR spans were returned, so it remains an unconfirmed hypothesis rather than the root cause (evidence 0f61e03e, c2e0f1c1). root_cause is null because no object was shown to be the origin of the sustained 503 connection terminations.

claims.text: Spans of frontend-proxy operation "ingress" carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR throughout 04:15–05:02; increase over a 10-minute lookback ranged from about 2.1 to 15.8 error spans (peak 15.79 in the window ending 04:38:40), and the computed 5-minute ingress error ratio peaked at 0.0033 (0.33%) at 04:38:40.

The frontend-proxy container log records 503 responses with response flag UC and detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} for requests routed to the frontend upstream, sporadically between 04:13:34 and 04:51:45 (examples at 04:13:34/35, 04:17:25 x2, 04:20:27, 04:24:05, 04:25:03, 04:29:13, 04:29:30 x3, 04:31:18, 04:32:17, 04:36:15, 04:37:09, 04:42:12, 04:42:43, 04:47:31, 04:50:59, 04:51:45 x2).

At 04:36:15–04:36:19 frontend-proxy logged a 503 UC reset at 04:36:15.360 and six HTTP 500 responses with detail via_upstream (04:36:19.285–04:36:19.885) for GET /api/products/LS4PSXUNUM, 2ZYFJ3GM2N, HQTGWGPNH4, L9ECAV7KIM and POST /api/checkout, plus another 503 UC at 04:37:09.331.

Two sampled traces of these 503s (trace ca40adbdde72b6db14d089defa3f1936 and trace 84bc3b40f6bcc436a1036e5d005bfe83) contain load-generator GET span with http.status_code 503/otel.status_code ERROR, frontend-proxy "ingress" span with http.status_code 503, and frontend-proxy "router frontend egress" span with error="true" and http.status_code 0 at 147–173 ms duration; no frontend service span appears in either sampled trace.

Deployment product-catalog was rolled out at 04:36:15: its pod template carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T04:36:15Z; events show ReplicaSet product-catalog-55f64b54c9 SuccessfulCreate and Deployment ScalingReplicaSet 0->1 at 04:36:15, pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 Started at 04:36:18, pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp Killing and ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete at 04:36:19, Deployment ScalingReplicaSet 1->0 at 04:36:19; the new and old ReplicaSets carry the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog and the same env values.

frontend's own error spans (operations GET, POST, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout and tcp.connect) are non-zero only in the window covering about 04:33–04:42 (about 5.5 error spans per 5-minute lookback) and are zero at the other sampled points from 04:14 to 05:03; frontend's overall error ratio peaked at only 0.0006 in that period.

ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) sets productCatalogFailure defaultVariant to "on" ("Fail product catalog service on a specific product"); every other fault/error/latency flag in that file (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, recommendationCacheFailure) is "off".

The metric query for service_name=product-catalog returned only two call series, both with status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET (oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts) over 04:14–05:02; that query returned no ERROR-status series for product-catalog.

Pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw (podIP 100.96.3.42) and pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-mzj56 (podIP 100.96.3.19) are both Running and Ready with restartCount 0, startedAt 04:03:16/04:03:17, and empty lastState; all otel-demo Deployments report available=1, ready=1.

frontend container has a CPU limit of 0.1 cores while observed CPU usage was about 0.09–0.10 cores, and 24–32% of its CFS periods were throttled across 04:14–04:56; frontend-proxy's throttle ratio was only about 3–5% and its limit is 0.03 cores.

Services frontend, frontend-proxy and product-catalog each have a selector and exactly one ready endpoint at query time (frontend 100.96.3.42:8080, frontend-proxy 100.96.3.19:8080, product-catalog 100.96.4.33:8080), with no notReadyAddresses.

The sporadic 503 UC failures are most consistent with the frontend HTTP server terminating a reused/keep-alive upstream connection before it responds (Envoy detail connection_termination, failures completing in ~147–176 ms, and no frontend server span in the sampled 503 traces). This cannot be confirmed because frontend's keep-alive/server timeout settings live in the container image and frontend application logs are not retrievable.

frontend CPU saturation (usage pinned at its 0.1-core limit with 24–32% CFS throttling) may contribute to aborted or delayed requests; however the throttle ratio is flat across the sampled window and does not line up with individual 503 timestamps, and there is no pre-04:13 baseline, so this remains unproven.

The flagd setting productCatalogFailure=on is a fault-injection candidate that could make product pages fail, but it does not match the observed path for this alert: the recurring frontend-proxy failures are 503 connection terminations rather than 500s for one specific product, the only 500 burst hit four different product IDs within 0.6 s at the product-catalog pod swap, and the product-catalog call series returned carried only UNSET status. It therefore remains an unconfirmed candidate rather than the root cause.

frontend-proxy's own pod is healthy (Running/Ready, restartCount 0, no lastState termination), its CFS throttling is only ~3–5%, and its recorded errors are on spans that proxy responses from the frontend upstream; the alert therefore reflects failures observed at frontend-proxy, not a crash of frontend-proxy itself.

The product-catalog pod change at 04:36 was a controller-driven rollout, not damage: ReplicaSet product-catalog-55f64b54c9 SuccessfulCreate plus old ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc SuccessfulDelete and Deployment ScalingReplicaSet events at 04:36:15/04:36:19, replacement pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 Running/Ready with restartCount 0, same image digest path and env as the previous ReplicaSet, with no Evicted or OOMKilled signal.

The 04:36:15 product-catalog rollout restart is not the sole cause of the alert: 503 UC connection terminations were already logged at 04:13:34 and continue at 04:42:12, 04:42:43, 04:47:31, 04:50:59 and 04:51:45, and the alert starts at 04:43:40, after the last rollout-related 500 response at 04:36:19.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate rule definition is not available: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with type=alert both returned nothing, so the exact expression, evaluation interval and the reported value 0.0111 could not be reproduced; my computed 5-minute ingress error ratio peaked at 0.0033.
frontend's application logs could not be read: fetches for container frontend returned 0 lines (bytes_read 0), so frontend-side error messages, crashes or connection handling cannot be inspected.

frontend's keep-alive/headers/request timeout settings are not exposed in any readable ConfigMap or env var (they live in the ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend image), so the connection-termination mechanism cannot be verified.

Jaeger retained no traces after about 04:32:10 (searches for frontend-proxy and frontend in 04:40–04:50, 04:58–05:03 returned nothing, and the newest returned traces end at 04:31:19), so the 04:36 500 burst and later 503s have no trace-level view.

The product-catalog pod log query for error/OLJCESPC7Z/productCatalog/flag/GetProduct keywords over 04:36–04:52 returned no matching lines (only 'Product Found', 'Reloading Product Catalog...', 'Loaded 10 products' were present in that window); an empty match is not proof of absence, and the old pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp's logs no longer exist.
Who or what triggered the product-catalog rollout restart at 04:36:15Z cannot be determined: the change_history integration is not available and no user/automation identity appears in the events.
No metric samples exist before 04:13:40 for the frontend-proxy error series or the frontend CPU-throttling series, so no pre-incident baseline exists for a latency or throttling trend claim.
next_steps: Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alerting rule (expression, lookback window and evaluation interval) from the alerting Prometheus/Alertmanager so the reported 0.0111 can be tied to a specific aggregation.

Compare the frontend server's keep-alive/headers timeout values with the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream idle timeout, and consider configuring the proxy upstream idle timeout below the server keep-alive timeout to remove the connection-reset race.

Verify whether the 04:36:15 rollout restart of Deployment product-catalog was intentional, and confirm the deployment's maxUnavailable/maxSurge settings give zero-downtime replacement for a 1-replica service.

Review whether flagd's productCatalogFailure flag is intentionally left at variant "on"; if not, set it back to "off" and confirm with product-catalog error spans/logs that no single-product failure occurs.
Consider raising the frontend container CPU limit (currently 0.1 cores with usage pegged at the limit and 24–32% CFS throttling) and re-check whether frontend-proxy 503 UC resets subside.
